Your Guide & Founder

Dennis's Story

I'm Dennis Taligoola, and I've been fortunate enough to call the East African wilderness my home for over a decade. My journey began not in a classroom, but on the open savannas of the Maasai Mara, where I first learned to read the land, track animals, and understand the delicate balance of nature.

Growing up near the edge of Kenya's wildlife corridors, I was captivated by the stories my grandfather shared about the great herds and the changing seasons. That childhood wonder never left me. Instead, it grew into a deep passion for wildlife conservation and a desire to share these incredible experiences with others.

What drives me each day is simple: the look of pure awe on a guest's face when they witness their first lion hunt, or the quiet moment of connection when we track elephants through the bush. Safari isn't just about ticking off the Big Five—it's about understanding the intricate web of life that makes Africa so extraordinary.

My favorite moments? They're often the unexpected ones: a leopard cub playing in a tree at dawn, sharing stories with Maasai elders under the stars, or watching a family of cheetahs teach their young to hunt. These are the experiences I live for, and the ones I'm honored to share with you.

East Africa Safari Destinations

Explore East Africa's premier national parks and reserves, each offering unique wildlife experiences

DESTINATIONS

East Africa's Wildlife Havens

East Africa is blessed with an incredible range of wildlife habitats - from the iconic savannahs of the Masai Mara to the dense forests of Uganda. Each destination offers visitors a unique perspective on Africa's remarkable biodiversity.

Our expertly guided safaris visit the most spectacular parks and reserves across Kenya and Tanzania, where you'll have the opportunity to witness the circle of life unfold in front of your eyes. Whether you're seeking the Big Five, the Great Migration, or specialized wildlife, we know where to find it.

Multiple countries
Year-round safaris
Diverse ecosystems
Conservation focused

Safari Regions

Kenya and Tanzania's diverse regions offer unique landscapes and wildlife viewing opportunities

DESTINATIONS

Top Safari Destinations

Explore East Africa's most spectacular wildlife viewing areas with our expert guides

Central Highlands, Kenya

Aberdares

The Aberdare National Park in the central highlands of Kenya retains an air of mystery - you can only imagine what undiscovered creatures still lurk here, such as rare Black Leopards.

Best time to visit:

January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Southern Kenya

Amboseli

Amboseli National Park covers 400 km² of plains redeemed by the stunning spectacle of Kilimanjaro towering over it.

Best time to visit:

January, February, June, July, August, September and October

Northern Tanzania

Lake Manyara

Lake Manyara National Park is one of Tanzania’s most dramatically located wildlife areas, consisting of a shallow soda lake at the foot of the Great Rift Valley’s western escarpment.

Best time to visit:

January, February, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Rift Valley, Kenya

Lake Naivasha

Lake Naivasha is one of Africa’s most renowned freshwater lakes, located in Kenya’s Great Rift Valley.

Best time to visit:

January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Rift Valley, Kenya

Lake Nakuru

Lake Nakuru National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is one of Africa’s premier safari destinations.

Best time to visit:

January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Southwest Kenya

Maasai Mara

The Maasai Mara National Reserve, covering 1,115 km² of rolling grasslands and riverine forests, is Kenya’s most iconic safari destination.

Best time to visit:

July, August, September and October

Northern Tanzania

Ngorongoro

Ngorongoro, often referred to as the eighth wonder of the world, is the world’s largest intact volcanic caldera that isn’t underwater.

Best time to visit:

January, February, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Northern Kenya

Samburu

Lying on the edge of northern Kenya's arid savannahs, the Samburu National Reserve appeals to both safari first-timers and veterans.

Best time to visit:

January, February, March, June, July, August, September, October and December

Northern Tanzania

Serengeti

Tanzania's oldest and most popular national park, the Serengeti is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and recently proclaimed one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the world.

Best time to visit:

January, February, June, July, August, September, October, November and December

Northern Tanzania

Tarangire

Named after the Tarangire River, which runs through the park and serves as the only water source for wildlife during the dry season, Tarangire National Park is a must-visit safari destination in northern Tanzania.

Best time to visit:

June, July, August, September, October and November

Southeastern Kenya

Tsavo East & Tsavo West

Tsavo East and Tsavo West together form one of the largest national parks in the world, covering almost 22,000 sq km.

Best time to visit:

January, February, March, April, August, September, October and November

Tanzania Coast

Zanzibar

Zanzibar, an archipelago off the coast of Tanzania, is famed for its stunning white sand beaches, turquoise waters, and rich cultural heritage.

Best time to visit:

January, February, June, July, August, September, October and December

WHEN TO VISIT

Best Time to Visit East Africa

Whether you prefer dramatic landscapes, wildlife spectacles, or peaceful escapes, East Africa offers unforgettable experiences year-round.

🌞 Dry Season (June – October)

Ideal for safaris — animals gather around water sources, and vegetation is sparse, improving visibility. Expect clear skies, cooler temperatures, and incredible action in the Masai Mara during the Great Migration.

Wildebeest river crossings (Jul–Oct)
Excellent visibility for big game
Comfortable temperatures, minimal rain
Best time for first-time safari-goers

🌿 Green Season (November – May)

Lush and vibrant, the green season is quieter and more affordable. Great for birders, photographers, and those who appreciate dramatic skies and fewer crowds.

Beautiful green landscapes
Bird migrations and baby animals
Stunning cloudscapes and soft light
Lower rates and fewer visitors

🐾 Migration Season

July–October in Masai Mara for dramatic river crossings.

🦁 Best Wildlife Viewing

June–October dry season offers peak game spotting.

📸 Best Photography

Green season (Nov–Dec, Mar) for lush backdrops and vivid skies.

💰 Best Value

Travel in April–May or November for savings and serenity.

Aberdares

Central Highlands, Kenya

OVERVIEW

About Aberdares

The Aberdare National Park in the central highlands of Kenya retains an air of mystery - you can only imagine what undiscovered creatures still lurk here, such as rare Black Leopards. The Aberdare National Park covers most of the highlands of Kenya. This beautifully scenic region is much cooler than the savannahs and offers a completely different perspective on the country. Game viewing is more challenging making sightings unexpected surprises. The scenery is spectacular with its mountainous terrain covered in thick tropical forests swathed in mist. At 10,000ft (3,000m), the bamboo gives way to moorland, home to eland, spotted and melanistic serval cats. Other features are the giant alpine varieties of lobelia, groundsel and heather. Ideal for walking, picnics, camping and trout fishing in the rivers, the moorlands are reminiscent of the European highlands.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Aberdares

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Mountain Scenery

The beautiful mountain scenery is one of the highlights of a visit to this National Park with spectacular mountainous terrain covered in thick tropical forests.

Waterfalls

The park has several picturesque waterfalls cascading through the misty mountain landscape, creating breathtaking scenic views.

Rare Wildlife

Rare animals including Black Serval, Black Leopard (seldom seen) and the Eastern Bongo (a huge forest Antelope) make this park truly special.

Amboseli

Southern Kenya

OVERVIEW

About Amboseli

Amboseli National Park covers 400 km² of plains redeemed by the stunning spectacle of Kilimanjaro towering over it. The snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro rising above a saucer of clouds dominates every aspect of Amboseli. Amboseli is one of Kenya's most popular parks, with great wildlife viewing all year round. The area includes Amboseli and Chyulu Hills National Parks, Maasai communities, and wildlife sanctuaries. Proximity to Nairobi and ease of access have made it a busy park with many lodges and hotels nearby. It is also home to the Maasai people, proud nomads known for living in harmony with the environment and wildlife.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Amboseli

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Mount Kilimanjaro Views

The majestic snow-capped peak of Mount Kilimanjaro forms a stunning backdrop to Amboseli, providing spectacular views for wildlife photography.

Elephant Paradise

Home to over 1,000 elephants, including some of Africa’s largest tuskers, Amboseli is famous for its impressive elephant herds and excellent opportunities to observe their behavior.

Observation Hill

A panoramic viewpoint offering 360-degree views of the park, wildlife-rich plains, and Mount Kilimanjaro.

Swamplands Wildlife

Permanent swamps attract diverse wildlife, including hippos, buffalo, and numerous bird species year-round.

Maasai Culture

Experience traditional Maasai villages (manyattas), learning about their culture, sustainable coexistence with wildlife, and nomadic lifestyle.

Big Five Wildlife

See four of the Big Five—lions, leopards, buffalo, and elephants—with occasional sightings of endangered black rhino.

Why These Months?

June to October and January to February are the best times to visit Amboseli. Dry seasons concentrate animals around swamps and water sources, improving wildlife viewing. Clear skies offer the best views of Mount Kilimanjaro, especially early morning and late afternoon. Roads are in better condition and vegetation is less dense, enhancing visibility.

GETTING THERE

How to Get to Amboseli

Transportation options to reach this incredible destination

By Road

Approximately 4 hours from Nairobi

Drive south via the Nairobi-Mombasa highway and local roads. The main park access is via Namanga on the Nairobi-Arusha Road (240 km), with tarmac up to Namanga and murram roads beyond. Alternative route via Emali (228 km) on the Nairobi-Mombasa Road, tarmac up to Emali then murram to Remito Gate. Access from Mombasa mainly through Tsavo West via Kimana Gate.

By Air

Around 45 minutes from Nairobi

Daily scheduled flights to Amboseli airstrip at Empusel Gate and light aircraft airstrips at Park Headquarters (Olekelunyiet), Kilimanjaro Buffalo Lodge, and Namanga town. Charter flights are also available.

Lake Manyara

Northern Tanzania

OVERVIEW

About Lake Manyara

Lake Manyara National Park is one of Tanzania’s most dramatically located wildlife areas, consisting of a shallow soda lake at the foot of the Great Rift Valley’s western escarpment. The lake takes up much of the park, leaving a narrow strip of land along its shores where game concentrates. This varied habitat attracts a wide variety of wildlife including one of Africa’s largest concentrations of elephants and large flocks of flamingos drawn by the lake’s algae.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Lake Manyara

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Tree-Climbing Lions

Lake Manyara is famous for its unique tree-climbing lions—view a pride resting in acacia trees, a rare and remarkable sight.

Flamingo Spectacle

Thousands of flamingos create striking pink carpets along the alkaline lake shores during peak seasons.

Birdlife Diversity

Nearly 400 bird species have been recorded, making it an excellent and accessible introduction to East African birds, including birds of prey.

Large Elephant Herds

One of Africa's largest elephant populations roams the park, providing excellent viewing opportunities.

Hippos and Crocodiles

Boat cruises offer chances to see pods of snorting hippos and basking crocodiles in the lake and rivers.

Maasai Mara

Southwest Kenya

OVERVIEW

About Maasai Mara

The Maasai Mara National Reserve, covering 1,115 km² of rolling grasslands and riverine forests, is Kenya’s most iconic safari destination. Often referred to as the "Seventh Wonder of the World," it is famed for the Great Migration, where over 1.3 million wildebeest and hundreds of thousands of zebras and gazelles cross from the Serengeti between July and October. The Mara is a year-round haven for wildlife, with all members of the Big Five and 95 species of mammals, amphibians, and reptiles. It also inspired the book and film "Out of Africa", cementing its global fame.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Maasai Mara

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Great Migration River Crossings

Witness the dramatic river crossings where over a million wildebeest and other herbivores brave crocodile-infested waters in their epic annual journey.

Big Five Wildlife

Home to lions, leopards, elephants, rhinos, and buffalo—making the Mara one of Africa’s top destinations for seeing the Big Five.

Hot Air Balloon Safaris

Soar above the plains at sunrise for breathtaking views of wildlife and landscapes, followed by a champagne breakfast.

Maasai Cultural Villages

Visit traditional Maasai villages to experience indigenous culture, crafts, and their unique coexistence with wildlife.

Mara River

This vital waterway is home to hippos and crocodiles, and serves as a crossing point for the Great Migration.

Cheetah Sightings

Open plains make it easy to spot cheetahs—one of the few places in Kenya where you can reliably see these sleek predators in action.

Samburu

Northern Kenya

OVERVIEW

About Samburu

Lying on the edge of northern Kenya's arid savannahs, the Samburu National Reserve appeals to both safari first-timers and veterans. The Ewaso Ng'iro River flows through doum palm groves and thick riverine forests, providing vital water for the reserve's game in this arid environment. Samburu offers first-class game viewing alongside adventure activities and fascinating cultural interactions. It is also historically significant as one of the areas where conservationists George and Joy Adamson raised Elsa the Lioness, made famous by the book and movie Born Free. The Samburu people, closely related to the Maasai, are herders of camels and goats, often seen on reserve boundaries bringing their animals to water. Known for their striking red shukas, beaded jewelry, and ochre-daubed hairstyles, the young Samburu men (Moran) have a reputation for glamour, prowess, and ferocity.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Samburu

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Samburu Special Five

Encounter rare northern specialist species including Grevy’s zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, gerenuk, and beisa oryx.

Ewaso Ng'iro River

The lifeline of the reserve flowing through palm groves and riverine forests, attracting elephants, large predators, and abundant birdlife.

Samburu Culture

Experience the traditions of the Samburu people, who maintain a semi-nomadic lifestyle and share close cultural ties with the Maasai.

Large Elephant Herds

Famous for large herds of elephants seen bathing and drinking along the riverbanks.

Wildlife & Predators

Home to lions, leopards, cheetahs, wild dogs, and Kamunyak the miracle lioness who adopted a baby oryx.

Bird Watching

Over 450 bird species including the Somali ostrich, golden-breasted starling, and vulturine guineafowl.

Ngorongoro

Northern Tanzania

OVERVIEW

About Ngorongoro

Ngorongoro, often referred to as the eighth wonder of the world, is the world’s largest intact volcanic caldera that isn’t underwater. This breathtaking natural amphitheater, with walls rising nearly 2,000 feet into the sky, supports the densest population of large animals on Earth and mirrors the ecosystems of the greater Serengeti within its 10-mile wide basin. Ngorongoro offers a rare blend of spectacular wildlife, dramatic scenery, and Maasai culture, making it one of the most iconic safari destinations in Africa.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Ngorongoro

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Ngorongoro Crater

The massive volcanic caldera harbors a self-contained ecosystem and is home to an extraordinary density of wildlife, including the Big Five.

Big Five Viewing

One of the easiest places in Africa to see all Big Five, including the endangered black rhino, often spotted in the morning forests.

Lake Makatare & Flamingos

A haven for migratory birds, Lake Makatare hosts thousands of flamingos and provides great birdwatching opportunities.

Hippo Pools

Spot hippos cooling off in the muddy swamps scattered across the crater floor, especially during hotter days.

Maasai Villages

Visit traditional Maasai settlements along the crater rim and learn about their coexistence with wildlife and pastoral culture.

Olduvai Gorge

An important paleoanthropological site, often called the Cradle of Mankind, offering insight into early human history.

Why These Months?

The best time to visit Serengeti National Park is from June to September, when wildlife is easiest to spot and the weather is dry and comfortable. This period offers excellent general wildlife viewing, though it's important to consider the timing of the Great Migration when planning your trip. The high season runs from July to March, during which the Ngorongoro Crater tends to attract large crowds. April and May mark the low season—these are the quietest months in the crater but also the wettest, with heavy rainfall making some roads challenging. The most favorable weather occurs from June to October, while March and April bring the heaviest rains and are generally considered the least ideal months to visit.

Charter flights are available to the Lake Manyara airstrip, followed by a short drive to the crater. Helicopter scenic flights are also an option.

OVERVIEW

About Serengeti

Tanzania's oldest and most popular national park, the Serengeti is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and recently proclaimed one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the world. It is famed for its annual Great Migration, when about six million hooves pound the open plains as over 200,000 zebras and 300,000 Thomson’s gazelles join more than a million wildebeest trekking for fresh grazing. The migration follows an ancient instinct, flowing south during the short rains (October-November) and moving west and north after the long rains (April-June), overcoming rivers and predators along the way. Even outside migration season, the Serengeti offers world-class game viewing with large herds of buffalo, elephants, giraffes, and thousands of antelope species.

ATTRACTIONS

Top Attractions in Serengeti

Discover the unique wildlife and landscapes that make this destination special

Great Migration

Witness the spectacular annual migration of millions of wildebeest, zebras, and gazelles crossing vast plains and rivers.

Abundant Wildlife

Home to lions, leopards, elephants, buffalo, cheetahs, African wild dogs, and many antelope species including Thomson’s and Grant’s gazelles.

Kopjes Rock Formations

Ancient granite and gneiss outcroppings like the popular Simba Kopje provide shelter and vantage points for wildlife.

Ol Doinyo Lengai Volcano

The only active volcano in the area, erupting unique white carbonatite lava that hardens into calcium-rich rock.

Bird Watching

Over 500 bird species including ostrich, secretary bird, kori bustard, crowned crane, marabou stork, and martial eagle.

Grumeti River Crossings

Watch dramatic wildebeest river crossings, where crocodiles await during migration season.

Why These Months?

The best times to visit Serengeti National Park are December to March and June to October. January and February coincide with wildebeest calving, while June to September offer great general wildlife viewing with chances to see the wildebeest crossing the Grumeti River (June-July). The high season runs from July to March, especially crowded around the Seronera area, while April and May are the low season with fewer visitors. The best weather occurs from June to October with little rainfall, while March and April mark the peak wet season.
